pairs/grid: In self-attention, every token scores every token, itself included. Cats like fish: three tokens asking, three answering, a grid of nine scores.
pairs/T: With T tokens, the grid is T by T, T squared scores: the matrix that Q times K transpose makes.
pairs/double: Now double the context, the tokens that attention reads at once. Four tokens make sixteen scores; eight make sixty-four.
pairs/why: Twice as many tokens ask, and each asks twice as many: two times two, four times the scores.
pairs/square: Ten times the tokens, a hundred times the scores. Growing with the square like this is called quadratic, from the Latin for squared.
grows/rows: Not everything grows that fast. The queries, keys and values have one row per token: twice the tokens, twice the rows.
grows/weights: The weights that make them, W Q, W K and W V, are shared by every token, so they stay the same size. Only the scores pair tokens up.
grows/vaswani: Ashish Vaswani and colleagues weighed this cost in 2017, in Attention Is All You Need. Over all the heads, each pair of tokens costs about d multiplications, d being a token's length, so attention's work grows like T squared, times d.
grows/rnn: A recurrent network of the same width pays per token instead: each step multiplies its state by a d by d matrix, so its work grows like T, times d squared.
grows/cross: So attention was the cheaper one while there were fewer tokens than d. With d at five hundred twelve, that held for most sentences in translation, their task.
memory/bytes: The scores take memory, too. A computer counts memory in bytes, and here each score is stored in two bytes.
memory/one: A thousand tokens make a thousand times a thousand scores: a million.
memory/mb: At two bytes each, that is two million bytes: two megabytes, as a megabyte is a million bytes.
memory/long: Make the context eight times longer, eight thousand tokens, and the scores grow sixty-four times: a hundred and twenty-eight megabytes, for one head.
memory/heads: And every head keeps its own grid. Sixteen heads hold about two gigabytes: two billion bytes.
memory/layer: Heads side by side, reading the same tokens, make a self-attention layer, just as neurons side by side make a layer.
memory/child: In 2019, Rewon Child and colleagues, modelling images, sound and text tens of thousands of steps long, opened their paper with this very cost: time and memory that grow quadratically with the length.
memory/end: That square is why long inputs are expensive for attention: twice the context, four times the work and the memory.
